name: muhsin
about:
I'm Muhsin, studying Artificial Intelligence at FH Hagenberg. Most of my skills are self-taught, and I learn best by building things. I'm interested in using AI and computational models to simulate brain processes and behaviour, understand how different brains may work in conditions such as neurodivergence, personality disorders, and schizophrenia, and explore how different treatments might affect them. Ultimately, I want to use these models to understand mental health better and find better ways to help people.

For this reason, and to develop a better understanding of these areas, I plan to attend medical school after my AI degree and continue learning about medicine, neuroscience, and psychiatry. My long-term goal is to combine AI, medicine, and neuroscience through computational psychiatry.

I also enjoy building practical AI solutions. This includes fine-tuning models for specific tasks, preparing and cleaning data for fine-tuning, and building AI applications using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, and others. I'm particularly interested in local AI and getting the most out of smaller models for specific tasks instead of always relying on larger models. I like experimenting, tinkering with models, and trying different approaches to see what works.

I'm also a strong advocate for mental health, suicide prevention, and child abuse prevention. I write more about these topics, as well as my own thoughts and experiences, in the blog section.

Outside of tech, I like being close to nature, spending time with cats, working out at the gym, and thrifting.
